title: 'I'm telling the truth': Earl Spencer defends Diana book claims about Charles in BBC interview
partialText: Princess Diana's brother tells the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg that "we'll forget her soon enough" were "exactly" the words used by the then-Prince of Wales.

title: Watch: Diana's brother says Charles 'went ballistic' in phone call after her death
partialText: Earl Spencer spoke exclusively with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg about claims he has made in a new book.

title: MI5 accepts it gave evidence based on lies in neo-Nazi spy case
partialText: It is the first time MI5 has confirmed the BBC's revelation that it gave evidence based on lies in court while defending the violent informant.

title: Flight chaos caused by software defect in space of a millisecond, report says
partialText: The failure led to more than 2,000 flights being cancelled and hundreds of thousands of passengers affected.

title: Teen who piloted Channel boat with 165 migrants jailed
partialText: Chan Mathok Atak has been sentenced to two years and three months in prison after piloting the boat.

title: Brother didn't match description of 'Putney pusher', suspect's sisters tell BBC
partialText: Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Nicholas Brandram's sisters accused the Metropolitan Police of being "negligent and reckless".

title: 'Get in' - woman joins police chase by giving officer a lift in Nissan Micra
partialText: The suspect reverse-rammed a police car and crashed into parked cars while trying to escape.

title: Tenko and Coronation Street actress Stephanie Cole dies aged 84
partialText: She was best known for playing Dr Beatrice Mason in the 1980s BBC wartime TV drama Tenko.

title: Men lose appeal for harrassing BBC journalist over A Very British Cult documentary
partialText: Kristofer Deichler, Jatinder Kamra and Sukhraj Singh were given community service and restraining orders for their harassment of Catrin Nye.

title: Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary apologises over 'high-fare rapists' remarks
partialText: O'Leary described his choice of language as "careless" and said "it won't happen again".

title: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron
partialText: The French president says he has tasked the government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children
partialText: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.

title: War may be coming. Are we psychologically ready?
partialText: The military and government say the risk of conflict is growing, but we may not be mentally ready for it

title: Why an American football game played the Canadian national anthem
partialText: The field in Buffalo was decked out with the flags of both countries, as tensions simmer and a trade war escalates.

title: We bought our £242,000 home without a deposit - here's how
partialText: The share of UK mortgages with smaller deposits is the highest it's been since 2008. The BBC spoke to borrowers about how they manage the risks.

title: Resident Evil: The video game adaptation with a lot to prove
partialText: The video game adaptation is a hit with critics, but director Zach Cregger says the fan response surprised him.

title: Watch: Voting under way in Russian election tightly controlled by Kremlin
partialText: Russia's parliamentary elections are under way, the first since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: 'Complete despair': Afghan female medical students fear being sent home from Pakistan
partialText: Since 2023, hundreds of thousands of Afghans have been deported from Pakistan and over two million have left.

title: Learner drivers turn to YouTube and TikTok to cut costs - but instructors warn of risks
partialText: One learner says social media clips saved her money, but there was also misinformation online.

title: Police begin operation to move migrants from Ceuta beaches
partialText: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.

title: British rapper Sway dies aged 44
partialText: Sway, whose hits included Still Speedin' and Level Up, was living in Ghana at the time of his death.

title: Warren Buffett steps down after six decades at Berkshire - 'Father Time always wins'
partialText: Since taking control in 1965, Buffett grew a struggling textile mill into a global conglomerate.

title: 'Insufficient funds' to pay Brewdog creditors and unpaid wages after takeover deal
partialText: Administrators say about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and holiday pay and £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
partialText: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

title: Football club apologises for United 93 shirt advert
partialText: Oxford United apologises for the image, which features the call sign of one of the planes used in the 9/11 attacks.

title: Move faster to solve climate challenges, Prince William says
partialText: The Prince of Wales tells the BBC we need to "accelerate" in finding solutions to climate challenges as Earthshot nominees are unveiled.

title: Oxford apologise for United 93 shirt advert

title: Will England boss Tuchel 'embrace the chaos'?
partialText: After the World Cup, England boss Thomas Tuchel wanted greater control. Two months on, he is keen to "embrace the chaos" after naming his squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.

title: Gabriel, 15, in Barcelona amid speculation over future
partialText: Man Utd youngster JJ Gabriel travels to Barcelona as some of Europe's biggest clubs continue to vie for his signature.

title: Uefa & Concacaf demand Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members
partialText: Uefa and Concacaf issue a joint statement calling on Fifa to pay $10m from its cash reserves to each of the 211 member associations.
